serializedLocalizedConversation.mainText:
#bot.Expression.NoHappy
You: Thank you for that, but because you sprinted so fast to the bus, people were giving us weird looks. 
You: You ran so fast that you probably beat some world record.
Bot: Don’t worry. I only did it for a few seconds and at my speed no passersby had time to bring out his cellphone and record it.
You: Well, I’m glad to hear that…
You: Let’s just forget about it and enjoy our time here.
You: What do you think about this exhibition?
Bot: It’s good. I know what I’m looking at.
She’s still remembering these abstract paintings. I hope it didn’t tarnish her opinion on art forever.
You: Any thoughts about the first one?
Bot: People are gathered on a square. Their robes and furniture indicate that they are citizens of ancient Greece. They seem distressed with something.
Bot: I don’t understand something. It’s titled ‘Agora of Athens before the Battle of Marathon’, but it was painted in 2005. How did the author know how this historic event looked when it took place over 2000 years ago?
You: I’m sure he’s done some research about the topic and based on it he painted it.
Bot: No amount of archeological research would allow for such detailed depiction of an event. 
You: The author just let his imagination loose a little I guess.
Bot: Isn’t that just lying though? This whole painting is a sham. 
You: W-Well that’s his artistic interpretation.
Bot: Then he should title it ‘My interpretation of Agora of Athens before the Battle of Marathon’. 
You: What about the second painting?
Bot: There are so many trees, mountains and a lake. Is this painting of a fantasy genre?
You: No, actually this painting is based on the Rocky Mountains I think. Moraine Lake to be exact. I know this because my mom got a postcard with a similar view once.
Bot: Sky is too blue, it’s unrealistic, that’s what threw me off. The real sky is more grey and smokey.
Oh no…
You: In big cities the sky is grey and smokey, but there are a few places in the world where the sky is blue like that.
She never left the city so it's not surprising she was thinking like that.
Maybe someday we will go on a vacation to a place with clean air?
There would be a problem with getting a pass for going to an area protected from pollution though. She’s a sexbot after all and you need to go to the Environment Protection Bureau with your ID to apply for it.
It seems impossible for now…
